rules.check: Each source file with nontrivial logic has test coverage at the right boundary, unless the user explicitly authorizes omission. Prefer E2E tests of real use cases with real UI and real fixtures. Behavior that an existing or changed E2E test exercises needs no unit-test file; require a unit-test file only for logic that no real workflow can reach. Documentation, agent configuration/instructions, declarative registries, and trivial glue are exempt; existing shared-contract coverage may suffice for mechanical forwarding without duplicate wiring tests.

Each source class with nontrivial logic that no E2E workflow exercises maps to exactly one unit-test class. Do not request a unit-test class for behavior that an E2E test exercises through the real UI or a real fixture; preserve the trivial-glue exception and inspect existing shared-contract tests before requesting another class.
Each unit test mocks external dependencies at the imported subject boundary, using `mock.patch.object()` when patching object members.
Every changed skipped test has explicit user authorization and a tracking ticket or explanation.

Each actual unit test without `subTest` has one ordered `# Arrange`, `# Act`, `# Assert` cycle and one action under test, with no independent actions hidden in helpers or interleaved with assertions. Helpers, fixture preparation, cleanup, and an exception-assertion context do not themselves add Acts or require separate markers.
Each unit-test name follows `test_<action>_<condition>_<expected_outcome>` and states concrete behavior.

Each unit test asserts an observable contract that would detect a relevant regression. A weak-assertion finding identifies a plausible missed regression; non-null, callback, or call-count assertions are valid when they establish the contract, not defects by syntax alone.

Every changed behavioral branch has coverage at the appropriate boundary, unless the user explicitly authorizes omission. An E2E test that exercises the branch through a real use case is sufficient; do not request unit tests for callbacks, cleanup, or failure paths only because the E2E test does not isolate them. Request a unit test only for a changed branch that no real workflow or fixture can reach. Mechanical shared-factory forwarding alone does not require duplicate wiring tests.
Each `subTest` case has an identifying title and its own independent Arrange, Act, and Assert cycle.

Each changed test proves consumer behavior rather than merely repeating its setup, implementation logic, or repository declarations as expected values. Identify a concrete regression missed by the repeated expectation.

sources.section: What is Not a Good Test

rules.check: Each changed unit test remains deterministic in the full suite without ordering assumptions, leaked mutable state, arbitrary sleeps, or retries.

sources.section: What is Not a Good Test

rules.check: Command tests exercise `do()` and `undo()` in separate test methods.
Tests expecting exceptions use `self.assertRaises` or `self.assertRaisesRegex`, never manual `try`/`except` flags.

Tests presented as unit tests exercise isolated behavior rather than live UI or real multi-component workflows. A finding identifies the executed interaction or dependency crossing; UI-independent logic with mocked UI dependencies remains valid unit coverage. Paths, imports, immutable value types, and frame waits alone do not prove the boundary.
